content: Figure FIGREF45 suggests that LGBTQ groups experience greater denial of agency in the New York Times than the institution's in-group identifier American. Furthermore, people described as homosexual experience even more denial of agency than people who are described as gay, illustrating how these two terms differ with respect to dehumanization. Unlike the improving attitudes indicated by our analysis of negative evaluations of a target group, it appears that denial of agency increased over time for all LGBTQ groups. However, the relatively rapid change in agency for homosexual is consistent with our other results of this label's pejoration.
